title: Per-endpoint adaptive SLI envelopes and prioritized surge-shedding playbook
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Define and implement a pragmatic schema for per-endpoint SLI envelopes that adapts to request shape (token length, modality, priority) and a corresponding prioritized surge-shedding policy. Deliverables: (1) SLI envelope format and ingestion pipeline, (2) error-budget vending rules and priority bands for shedding, (3) automation for regional evacuation credits and fast-fail circuit triggers, (4) runbook and console dashboard slices for on-call operators.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI envelope spec checked into repo and linked from console config
Prometheus/OTel metrics emitted for all new SLI dimensions (p99 latency by token-bin, request-quality score, variant-priority)
Automated error-budget allocator honors priority bands and can reclaim credits across regions via the credit transfer API
Simulated chaos tests demonstrate controlled shedding under a 3x burst with zero silent-drop for P0 routes and graceful degradation for P2/P3 routes
Runbook pages updated with play-by-play for triage, manual override, and rollback of shedding policies
tasks: Draft SLI envelope JSON schema and schema registry entry
Implement agent that computes request-quality score at ingress and attaches to trace headers
Extend runtime admission controller to consult envelope + priority bands before enqueueing
Create error-budget vending service with per-variant counters and regional escrow support
Add dashboard tabs in Console: SLI envelope health, error-budget burn rate, active shed decisions
Author chaoskit scenario and run load tests against staging multi-region cluster
decisions: Use token-length bucketing (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512) rather than continuous percentiles for simpler runtime routing
Prioritization will use three bands: P0 (never shed), P1 (shed only under sustained high burn), P2/P3 (shed permissively)
Regional credit transfers will be conservative: at most 20% of donor region credits per 1h window to avoid cascades
Circuit thresholds based on weighted burn-rate + median latency rather than raw tail percentile to reduce sensitivity to noisier samples
risks: Misclassification of request priority could cause unnoticed drops for paying customers; mitigation: token-level audit logs and dry-run mode
Credit-transfer logic could exacerbate failures if donor region is under-reported; mitigation: require two independent telemetry signals before transfers
Increased metric cardinality due to token buckets could strain ingestion; mitigation: apply tag-rollup and retention policy
